n01: Four children under five came in today with watery diarrhoea and vomiting, all from Thaga Park. That's more than we usually see. Two of the mothers said the tap water smelled funny.
n02: Three small children under five with diarrhoea since yesterday, from Nonyana Flats. One mother says the tap water has been coming out brown.
n03: This morning I saw Thabo Mokoena and his sister Lerato, plus the neighbour's baby, Karabo. All three have vomiting and diarrhoea, and they live in Sefate Extension. Sister Dlamini at the other clinic says she's seeing the same.
n04: Quick one between patients. A few kids with fever and a rash on the face and body, starting over the last couple of days. Not sure if it's more than usual. One of them has measles, confirmed by the lab.
n05: Five adults came in this afternoon with sudden stomach cramps and vomiting, about two hours after eating vetkoek from the same spaza shop by the taxi rank in Leeba View. One of them is very weak.
n06: Two teenagers from Kgwedi Heights came in tonight with high fever, a stiff neck and confusion. That's unusual for us. They go to the same high school.
n07: Six older people, all over sixty, from Mmutla Ridge with bloody diarrhoea over the past week. The usual treatment isn't helping, and we're running low on rehydration salts.
n08: Lots of coughing and flu in Lebone Gardens this week, maybe ten adults. Same as usual for this time of year, really. What antibiotic should I be giving them?
n09: Three babies under one with diarrhoea from Thaga Park. And separately, two schoolchildren with red, itchy eyes from Leeba View. All since yesterday.
n10: Hello? Testing, testing. Is this recording? Okay, I'll call back later.
